dish: Tsukemen dipped in a rich pork-and-seafood broth simmered for 13 hours
n: Rokurinsha, Tokyo Ramen Street (六厘舎 東京ラーメンストリート)
address: Tokyo Ramen Street, Tokyo Station First Avenue B1 (Yaesu side), Marunouchi, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo
w: The star of Tokyo Station's eight-shop Tokyo Ramen Street and by far its longest queue — thick tsukemen noodles dipped into a dense pork-and-seafood broth simmered for 13 hours.

dish: Old-school Tokyo shōyu ramen with chewy noodles and fried onions, gyoza on the side
n: Chūkamen-ten Kiraku, Dōgenzaka (中華麺店 喜楽)
w: A Dōgenzaka relic serving Tokyo-style noodles since 1952 — shōyu ramen with chewy noodles and crisp fried onions, regulars coming back for decades.

dish: Shrimp tsukemen — shrimp-miso and shrimp-tomato dipping broths made from leftover shrimp shells
n: Tsukemen Gonokami Seisakusho (つけ麺 五ノ神製作所)
address: Sendagaya, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo (by Shinjuku Station south side)
w: Queues form an hour before opening for this shrimp-obsessed tsukemen counter, whose creamy shrimp-miso and shrimp-tomato dips are built from hundreds of kilos of otherwise-wasted shrimp shells.

dish: Hakata tonkotsu ramen — milky pork-bone broth with ultra-thin flat noodles
w: Founded in 1946 as the first Hakata-style ramen shop in the Kantō region; a late-night Nishi-Azabu institution for milky tonkotsu and ultra-thin flat noodles.

dish: Mabo ramen — noodles under fiery, numbing Sichuan mapo tofu
n: Shibire Noodles Rousokuya, Ginza (SHIBIRE NOODLE 蝋燭屋)
w: A chic Ginza noodle bar run by a former Chinese-restaurant chef, specialising in ma-la heat: mabo ramen crowned with numbing mapo tofu.

dish: Rustic shōyu ramen; shōyu/shio/white-shōyu tsukemen limited to 10 a day
n: Ramenya Shima, Nishi-Shinjuku (らぁ麺や 嶋)
w: Ranked No 1 on Ramen Adventures' best-100 for 2025 and a fixture of Tabelog's Tokyo top three — queues once began at 7am; the rustic shōyu ramen is the bowl to get.

dish: Double-soup (duck + seafood) chūka soba with a punchy shōyu tare
n: Chūka Soba Shibata, Komae (中華そば しば田)
w: A celebrated chūka-soba champion that relocated to Komae; its duck-and-seafood double soup and punchy soy tare put it at No 4 on Ramen Adventures' 2025 Tokyo best-100.

dish: Shōyu or shio chūka soba on kombu, dried-fish, duck and Shamo-chicken stock
n: Chūka Soba Kamofuku, Hachiōji (中華そば 鴨福)
address: Hachiōji, Tokyo (15 min walk from Hachiōji Station)
w: Western Tokyo's most raved-about ramen of 2024 per Time Out and No 5 on Ramen Adventures' 2025 best-100 — worth the trek from Hachiōji Station for its duck-and-Shamo chūka soba.

dish: Kirby-shaped burgers and pizza; each dish comes with a gift (plate, figurine, coaster or mug)
n: Kirby Café Tokyo, Tokyo Solamachi (カービィカフェ)
address: Tokyo Solamachi 4F, Tokyo Skytree Town, Oshiage, Sumida-ku, Tokyo
w: Nintendo's pink hero gets his own café on Solamachi's fourth floor under Skytree — Kirby-shaped burgers and pizza, most dishes and drinks served with a collectible, plus an exclusive-goods shop.
anime: Kirby (Nintendo / HAL Laboratory) — the official character café

dish: Tasting counters from ham and sausages to Japanese oden; Café Prunier Paris caviar and champagne
n: Isetan Shinjuku Depachika (伊勢丹新宿店 食品フロア)
address: Isetan Shinjuku main store B1, 3-14-1 Shinjuku, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo
w: The flagship Isetan's basement food hall — one of Tokyo's poshest depachika, renovated in 2023, with a fresh market of tasting counters (ham, sausage, oden) and Café Prunier Paris for caviar and champagne.

dish: Ready-made deli, wagashi and Western sweets on B2; one of Tokyo's best cheese counters and flawless Japanese fruit on B3
n: Ginza Mitsukoshi Depachika (銀座三越 食品フロア)
address: Ginza Mitsukoshi B2–B3, Ginza 4-chōme, Chūō-ku, Tokyo
w: Two basement floors under Ginza's landmark department store: B2 for prepared food, Japanese and Western sweets and bakeries; B3 a gourmet supermarket with an outstanding cheese counter and perfect Japanese fruit.

dish: Oden simmered in a light dashi, served since 1915
n: Asakusa Oden Otafuku (浅草おでん 大多福)
w: Founded in 1915 and one of Tokyo's oldest oden houses — paper lanterns, a kept garden and pots of oden simmering in light dashi; a former Michelin Bib Gourmand.

dish: Grilled-then-steamed unagi with a sauce unchanged for some 220 years
n: Unagi Komagata Maekawa (駒形 前川)
address: Komagata, Taitō-ku, Tokyo (on the Sumida River near Asakusa Station)
w: An Edo-period eel wholesaler turned restaurant on the Sumida riverbank: unagi grilled and steamed until fluffy, lacquered with a tare the house says has not changed in 220 years.

dish: Tendon (tempura over rice) and tempura sets
n: Daikokuya Tempura, Asakusa (大黒家天麩羅)
address: Near Sensō-ji (Denbōin-dōri side), Asakusa, Taitō-ku, Tokyo
w: A stone's throw from Sensō-ji, the best known of Asakusa's old tempura houses (alongside San Sada and Owariya), with queues for its tempura and tendon.

dish: Customisable Hakata tonkotsu ramen eaten in solo booths
w: The Fukuoka tonkotsu chain famous for customising noodle firmness, richness, garlic and spring onion on a paper form and slurping alone in a partitioned booth — a rite of passage for first-time visitors.

dish: Single-origin pour-over and espresso at Blue Bottle's first store outside the US
w: Blue Bottle's first café outside the US (2015), set in a converted warehouse — its arrival made Kiyosumi-Shirakawa Tokyo's specialty-coffee neighbourhood.

dish: Agemanjū (deep-fried bean-paste buns) and seasonal wagashi, in a 1930 shop
w: A 1930 sweets parlour that escaped wartime damage and still trades from its original wooden building, a designated historic structure — famous for agemanjū and old-school wagashi.

dish: Hand-kneaded, rolled and cut soba; yuba (tofu-skin) soba and mitsuba soba
address: Residential street ~10 min walk from Shimokitazawa Station, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo
w: A traditional house with a small garden on a quiet Shimokitazawa backstreet, drawing soba connoisseurs from across the city for hand-cut noodles — try the yuba soba or mitsuba soba.

dish: Vienna coffee (espresso topped with whipped cream)
w: Jimbōchō kissaten opened in 1949 in a narrow alley of the book town, a long-standing literary hangout; credited with introducing Vienna coffee to Japan.

dish: Morning set: coffee with butter toast
w: Iconic Jimbōchō kissaten in business since 1955, known for its cottage-style front and tiki-like interior crammed with trinkets gifted by regulars.

dish: Egg sandwich (tamago-sando) with coffee
w: Kissaten in a 1916 Yanaka building, run as a coffee shop from 1938 to 2006 and reopened in 2009 with the original exterior and signage; known for its egg sandwich.

dish: Hand-poured single-origin coffee (around ten bean varieties)
n: Arise Coffee Roasters (アライズコーヒーロースターズ)
w: Small single-origin roaster in an old corner shop in Kiyosumi-Shirakawa, Tokyo's coffee district; the owner hand-pours each cup and chats with regulars.

dish: Japanese whisky flights incl. rare Venture Whisky and Mercian bottlings
w: Tiny Nishi-Shinjuku whisky bar with about 300 bottles, over a hundred of them Japanese incl. sold-out limited editions; the cinephile owner screens silent films while you drink.

dish: House Endless Brown Ale from 40+ taps
n: Goodbeer Faucets Shibuya (グッドビアフォウセッツ 渋谷)
w: Shibuya craft-beer bar open since 2012 with one of the city's largest tap lists (40+ Japanese, US and European beers) and a well-known happy hour.

dish: Baird Teikoku IPA and Angry Boy Brown Ale
n: Baird Beer Nakameguro Taproom (ベアードタップルーム中目黒)
address: 2F Nakameguro Gate Town, 2-1-3 Kamimeguro, Meguro-ku, Tokyo
w: First Tokyo pub of Numazu's Baird Brewing, a brick-and-wood taproom pouring Baird's own beers alongside New Haven-style pizza.

dish: Azuki and meringue kakigōri (shaved ice with mochi sauce and cooked azuki)
n: Azuki to Kouri (あずきとこおり)
w: Seven-seat, reservation-only kakigōri counter in Yoyogi-Uehara opened in January 2022 by pastry chef Miho Horio (ex-Florilège); signature azuki-and-meringue shaved ice.

dish: Seasonal-fruit kakigōri accented with sake lees
w: Residential-Nakano shaved-ice shop of Asako Harada, the 'Kakigōri Queen' said to have eaten some 1,800 bowls in a year; known for mountainous, painterly bowls such as seasonal fruit with sake lees.

dish: Precisely warmed hot sake (kanzake) with a five-course omakase
w: Eight-seat counter izakaya a short walk from central Shibuya; the sake sommelier is a hot-sake specialist warming each pour to a precise temperature, paired with a good-value omakase.

dish: Coffee during the twice-daily classical record 'concerts'
n: Meikyoku Kissa Lion (名曲喫茶ライオン)
w: Tokyo's oldest and best-known classical-music café, first opened in 1926 and rebuilt in 1950; pew-like seats face a 3m Pioneer speaker wall and conversation is discouraged.

dish: Drip coffee in a family-run 1954 kissaten
w: Yotsuya kissaten started in 1954 by the father of current owner Hiroaki Ogura, profiled by Monocle among Tokyo's enduring independent kissaten; a regular haunt of visiting jazz band The Lagerphones.

dish: Drinks played against an 11,000-record jazz, blues and soul vinyl wall
w: Small Dogenzaka record bar whose name stands for Jazz, Blues and Soul; over 11,000 LPs line the walls and the owner spins from them.

dish: Mame-daifuku (mochi with red bean paste and salty whole beans)
w: Wagashi shop by Gokokuji Station renowned for its large mame-daifuku, mochi wrapped around anko with slightly salty whole beans kneaded in, still sold cheaply.

dish: Filter-coffee tasting courses from ~20 auction-lot single origins
w: Kuramae specialty coffee flagship offering tasting courses and around 20 filtered coffees, many rare single origins bought at auction, with an omakase-style coffee experience.

dish: Brownie flight of three single-origin cacao cakes; hot chocolate
n: Dandelion Chocolate Factory & Café Kuramae (ダンデライオン・チョコレート 蔵前)
w: Tokyo home of the San Francisco bean-to-bar chocolatier: half café, half factory, where you watch chocolate made through the glass and order the brownie flight.

dish: Siphon coffee; 'fruit' and 'chocolate' house blends
n: Obscura Coffee Roasters — Café Obscura, Sangenjaya (オブスキュラ コーヒーロースターズ)
w: Sangenjaya roaster founded in 2009 and credited with seeding the district's specialty coffee scene; its gallery-like main café specialises in siphon coffee with two house blends and rotating single origins.

dish: iekei ramen (tonkotsu-shoyu broth with spinach, nori and egg)
w: The shop that started iekei ramen in 1974 — the 家 in 'iekei' honours Yoshimura-ya; its tonkotsu-shoyu soup with spinach and nori spawned Yokohama's whole iekei style.

dish: unagi kabayaki / unajū (sauce unchanged since 1807)
w: Kawagoe eel house founded in 1807 whose secret kabayaki sauce has been passed down to the seventh generation; cited as serving one of Japan's most renowned grilled unagi.

dish: hōtō (thick flat noodles stewed in miso with kabocha and vegetables, one iron pot per person)
address: 2458 Higashi-Koiji, Funatsu, Fujikawaguchiko, Minamitsuru District, Yamanashi 〒401-0301
w: Fuji Five Lakes hōtō specialist that makes its flat noodles in house; each diner gets a giant pot of hōtō in miso broth with kabocha and cabbage, and queues are common. A second branch is at 2746-1 Kawaguchi, Fujikawaguchiko.

dish: Modern Edomae sushi balancing fat and char, served in a gallery-like room
n: Udatsu Sushi, Nakameguro (宇田津 鮨)
w: Hisashi Udatsu's art-gallery-like sushi counter hidden in Nakameguro's backstreets — textbook nigiri that sneaks in surprises, with paintings on the walls; listed in the MICHELIN Guide.

dish: Coffee roasted on site — espresso, nitro and tap milk tea, coffee cocktails and Princi bakes
address: On the Meguro River, Aobadai, Meguro-ku, Tokyo
w: Opened March 2019 as the fifth and then-largest Starbucks Reserve Roastery: a four-floor Kengo Kuma building clad in Japanese cedar beside the Meguro River's cherry trees, roasting on site with coffee cocktails upstairs.

dish: Hanetsuki gyōza — pan-fried dumplings joined by a crisp lacy 'wing'
address: Near JR Kamata Station, Kamata, Ōta-ku, Tokyo
w: Where Dalian-born Isao Yagi invented hanetsuki ('winged') gyōza, pouring flour-water into the pan for a crisp lattice — the reason Kamata calls itself the birthplace of winged dumplings.

dish: Tonkatsu fried before you at a long counter round the open kitchen
w: Frying tonkatsu since 1939 with hardly a change: a long counter wraps the open kitchen so diners watch the cooks at work, and the benches round the room are always full of people queuing for a counter seat.

dish: Tofu kaiseki — signature warm tofu in dashi-seasoned soy milk, made daily in its own Okutama workshop
n: Tofuya Ukai, Shiba-kōen (とうふ屋うかい)
w: A samurai-era merchant's residence and carp-pond garden at the foot of Tokyo Tower (its 'borrowed scenery'), serving tofu kaiseki built on Hokkaido-bean tofu made each morning in the Okutama mountains.

dish: Shuzo Kishida's modern French carte-blanche tasting menu
address: 1F, Garden City Shinagawa Gotenyama, 6-7-29 Kitashinagawa, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo 141-0001
w: Chef Shuzo Kishida's modern French dining room in Gotenyama — one of Tokyo's eleven three-MICHELIN-star restaurants in the 2026 guide.

dish: Seiji Yamamoto's seasonal Japanese (kaiseki) tasting course
n: RyuGin, Tokyo Midtown Hibiya (日本料理 龍吟)
address: 7F, Tokyo Midtown Hibiya, 1-1-2 Yūrakuchō, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo 100-0006
w: Seiji Yamamoto's celebrated Japanese restaurant, moved from Roppongi to the 7th floor of Tokyo Midtown Hibiya — three MICHELIN stars in the 2026 guide.

dish: Ryōtei-style seasonal Japanese kaiseki in private rooms
n: Kioicho Fukudaya (紀尾井町 福田家)
w: A traditional ryōtei in Kioichō serving seasonal Japanese cuisine — two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 Tokyo guide.

dish: Edomae sushi omakase at Takahashi Harutaka's counter
w: Takahashi Harutaka's Ginza Edomae sushi counter — three MICHELIN stars ('exceptional cuisine') in the 2026 guide.

dish: Chef Kadowaki's seasonal Japanese tasting course
n: Azabu Kadowaki (麻布 かどわき)
w: Toshiya Kadowaki's Azabu-Jūban Japanese restaurant — three MICHELIN stars ('exceptional cuisine') in the 2026 guide.

dish: Chinese tasting menu paired with Chinese teas
w: Tomoya Kawada's Minami-Azabu Chinese restaurant in a quiet house — one of Tokyo's eleven three-MICHELIN-star restaurants in the 2026 guide.

dish: Classic French haute-cuisine tasting menu
w: Shiseido's historic Ginza French restaurant, opened in 1973 — three MICHELIN stars in the 2026 Tokyo guide.

dish: Shinobu Namae's innovative French tasting menu
n: L'Effervescence, Nishi-Azabu (レフェルヴェソンス)
w: Shinobu Namae's Nishi-Azabu restaurant fusing French technique and Japanese produce — three MICHELIN stars in the 2026 Tokyo guide.

dish: French haute-cuisine tasting menu in Robuchon's château
n: Joël Robuchon, Yebisu Garden Place (ジョエル・ロブション)
address: Yebisu Garden Place, 1-13-1 Mita, Meguro-ku, Tokyo
w: The late Joël Robuchon's flagship Tokyo dining room in the faux-château at Yebisu Garden Place (Meguro-ku side) — three MICHELIN stars in the 2026 guide.

dish: Edomae sushi omakase
n: Sushi Kanesaka, Ginza (鮨 かねさか)
w: Shinji Kanesaka's basement Ginza sushi counter, the mothership of a group with branches abroad — two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 guide.

dish: Chef's seasonal tasting course
w: A small Jingūmae restaurant holding two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 Tokyo guide.

dish: Chef's seasonal tasting course
w: Nakameguro restaurant promoted from one to two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 Tokyo guide.

dish: Wansashi — the classic pairing of sashimi and clear soup — within a seasonal Japanese course
w: Chef Yamamoto's basement Japanese restaurant in Mita — two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 guide; inspectors note that for all his innovations he stays true to tradition with wansashi, sashimi paired with soup.

dish: Chef's tasting course
w: Fine-dining restaurant in the Kabutochō financial quarter — two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 guide.

dish: Chef's tasting course
address: 3F, Tokyo Garden Terrace Kioichō, 1-3 Kioichō, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo 102-0094
w: Tasting-menu restaurant on the third floor of Tokyo Garden Terrace Kioichō — two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 guide.

dish: Chef's tasting course
w: Shintomi restaurant listed with two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 Tokyo guide.

dish: Japanese course built around charcoal-grilled ingredients
w: One-MICHELIN-star Kagurazaka Japanese restaurant whose forte is charcoal grilling, each ingredient handled with the strictest attention.

dish: Seasonal Japanese course in a no-nonsense style
w: 'In simple honesty' — a phrase handed down from the chef's two mentors names this one-MICHELIN-star Kagurazaka Japanese restaurant and its plain-spoken cooking.

dish: Japanese course paired with sake and chosen vessels
w: One-MICHELIN-star Kagurazaka restaurant aiming for the unexpected through a trinity of food, sake and serving vessels.

dish: Sushi omakase
w: Shinjuku 1-chōme sushi counter newly awarded one MICHELIN star in the 2026 Tokyo guide.

dish: Chef's tasting course
w: Asakusa restaurant holding one MICHELIN star ('high quality cooking') in the 2026 guide — the district's starred table beyond the tempura and unagi houses.

dish: Tuscan cooking — chicken-liver crostini, Florentine-style simmered tripe, pici in tomato ragù
w: A Bib Gourmand trattoria near Tomioka Hachimangū where the chef's love of Tuscany shows in chicken-liver crostini, Florentine tripe and hand-rolled pici.

dish: Seasonal Japanese course
w: A Japanese restaurant in shitamachi Morishita, selected by the MICHELIN Guide (2026 selection).

dish: Chinese cooking
w: A Chinese restaurant in Kiyosumi-Shirakawa's Miyoshi district, selected by the MICHELIN Guide (2026 selection).

dish: Contemporary tasting course
w: A contemporary restaurant in Sumida's Yokokawa district, selected by the MICHELIN Guide (2026 selection).

dish: Creative small plates built for sake, with meat dishes a fixture of the menu
w: A Bib Gourmand in residential Setagaya whose creative cooking is designed around its affinity with sake — meat dishes are an indispensable part of the menu.

dish: French bistro cooking
w: A French Bib Gourmand in Ikejiri, near Ikejiri-Ōhashi — good-value cooking in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide.

dish: French cooking
w: A French Bib Gourmand in the Kitazawa (Shimokitazawa) backstreets — good quality, good value cooking in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide.

dish: Kusa-dango (mugwort rice dumplings with red-bean paste) and river-fish dishes
address: Shibamata 7-chōme, Katsushika-ku, Tokyo (from Shibamata Station to Taishakuten)
w: The 200-metre Edo-era approach to Shibamata Taishakuten, lined with wooden shops selling the town's speciality kusa-dango and restaurants serving river fish such as eel and carp — the setting of the Tora-san films.

dish: Motsuyaki (grilled offal skewers), raw-style motsu and motsu stew at ¥200 a plate
address: 1-18-8 Tateishi, Katsushika-ku, Tokyo (inside Tateishi Nakamise arcade)
w: Tateishi's legendary motsuyaki counter in the post-war Nakamise arcade — a queue of 30 forms before the 2pm opening for grilled innards, stew and pickles at ¥200 a plate, with an ordering shorthand regulars help newcomers through.

dish: Sub-¥100 meat and vegetable skewers (Kabura-ya) and cheap draught in tiny bars
address: By Kita-Senju Station West Exit, Senju, Adachi-ku, Tokyo
w: A drinking alley off Kita-Senju's west exit that keeps the old yokochō charm — salarymen and Tokyo Denki University students pack its izakaya, where Kabura-ya grills skewers for under ¥100.

dish: Standing bar pouring from some 1,500 bottled beers
address: Nomiya Yokochō area by Kita-Senju Station West Exit, Adachi-ku, Tokyo
w: A bottle-shop-cum-standing-bar in Kita-Senju's drinking alley with around 1,500 bottled beers to drink on the spot.

dish: Maru menchi (deep-fried minced-beef cutlet) from the butcher counter; wagyu steak upstairs
w: A Kichijōji butcher whose ground-floor counter draws queues for its maru menchi croquettes, with a wagyu steak restaurant on the floor above.

dish: Single-origin pour-overs and a three-coffee tasting set; seasonal coffee-jelly latte and espresso mikan soda
address: 4-13-15 Kichijōji, Musashino, Tokyo (end of Nakamichi shopping street)
w: A blue-fronted micro-roastery opened in 2014 at the end of Kichijōji's Nakamichi street by two young roasters — single origins in signature blue cups, cuppings and roasting workshops.

dish: Flambéed kakigōri — shaved ice under meringue set alight at the table
w: Kichijōji's Alice-in-Wonderland-inspired café where shaved ice is cloaked in meringue and set on fire, the flaming sauce changing with the flavour.

dish: Niboshi ramen — dried-sardine broth boiled 12 hours, with curly and wide flat noodles
n: Sugoi Niboshi Ramen Nagi, Golden Gai (すごい煮干ラーメン凪)
address: 2F, Shinjuku Golden Gai (G2 Street), 1-1-10 Kabukichō, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo
w: Up a steep stair in an old wooden Golden Gai house, the Nagi chain's 2008 return to its birthplace serves pungent niboshi ramen from sardines boiled for 12 hours — open 24 hours.

dish: Korokke (croquettes) from 20-plus shops, plus yakitori, yakisoba and dango
n: Togoshi Ginza Shōtengai (戸越銀座商店街)
address: Togoshi, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo (around Togoshi-ginza Station, Tōkyū Ikegami line)
w: Tokyo's longest open-air shopping street — 1.3 km and some 400 shops — where more than 20 shops fry croquettes for snacking on the walk, between yakitori, yakisoba and dango stands.

dish: French bistro cooking
w: A French bistro near Jiyūgaoka from a chef schooled in both Tokyo and Paris kitchens — Bib Gourmand in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide.

dish: Cone-shaped Mont Blanc filled with liqueur-scented chestnut cream; Rihei-chestnut Mont Blanc on almond meringue
n: Mont St. Clair, Jiyūgaoka (モンサンクレール)
w: A patisserie in Jiyūgaoka, Tokyo's 'Little Europe' of sweet shops — its tall cone-shaped Mont Blanc and Rihei-chestnut version make Time Out's best Mont Blancs in Tokyo.

dish: Yakitori, curry and izakaya plates in a maze of tiny pubs and standing bars
address: A few minutes' walk from Sangenjaya Station, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo
w: Sangenjaya's 'triangle' — a maze of alleys a few minutes from the station packed with old-school and new-wave pubs, yakitori joints and curry counters, a very local yokochō that redevelopment has passed by.

dish: Herbal-infused spirits — ginger, goji, lemongrass, lavender, even broiled eel
w: A six-seat counter in the Sankaku Chitai triangle pouring spirits infused with medicinal herbs and oddities from goji berries and lavender to broiled eel.

dish: Fukagawa-meshi — asari clams in sweet Edo-style miso broth poured over rice (bukkake), or clams cooked into the rice (takikomi)
address: By Tomioka Hachimangū, Monzen-Nakachō, Kōtō-ku, Tokyo
w: The go-to for Fukagawa-meshi, the late-Edo fishermen's clam rice of this old fishing district — the poured-over version is made fresh to order with richly sweet miso and freshly harvested clams.

dish: Chanko-nabe (sumo wrestlers' hot pot) — lunch sets with a different chanko each day, e.g. pork-miso or duck-dumpling
n: Chanko Tomoegata, Ryōgoku (ちゃんこ巴潟)
w: Sumo town's favourite chanko-nabe house for nearly 50 years — the wrestlers' hot pot served as lunch sets that change by weekday (pork miso on Tuesdays, duck dumplings on Wednesdays) and by season.

dish: Duck shōyu ramen — Japanese duck and leek simmered two days into a clear stock, three-soy tare; duck tsukemen
w: One of Ueno's most popular ramen counters: only Japanese duck and leek, simmered for two days into a clear, sweet, ungamey stock with house-made noodles — the anchor of the Okachimachi 'ramen yokochō' cluster.

dish: Street snacks: Niku no Suzuki's all-beef menchi katsu, lucky-cat taiyaki at Manekiya, manjū and matcha
n: Yanaka Ginza Shōtengai (谷中銀座商店街)
address: Yanaka 3-chōme, Taitō-ku, Tokyo (between Nippori and Sendagi stations, below the Yūyake Dandan steps)
w: A 60-shop old-Tokyo shopping street between Nippori and Sendagi, best grazed: beef menchi katsu from Niku no Suzuki (since 1980), cat-shaped taiyaki, manjū and matcha, all below the 'sunset steps'.

dish: 'Wahaha' niboshi chūka soba — a gentle dried-sardine broth without the usual bitterness
w: Kokubunji's ramen standout, run by alumni of Nagi and Gamushara: the signature 'wahaha' niboshi chūka soba alongside a chicken 'gahaha' and an 'ahaha' tsukemen.

dish: Tsukemen served with a bamboo screen in the noodle bowl so the noodles never go soggy
n: Tsukemen Enji, Kichijōji (つけ麺 えん寺)
w: A hugely popular Kichijōji tsukemen shop and a food-magazine favourite, known for the bamboo mat in the noodle bowl that drains stray broth.

dish: Sawanoi sake — free brewery tour, then ten sakes by the cup at the riverside Sawanoi-en tasting room
n: Ozawa Shuzo — Sawanoi Sake Brewery, Ōme (小澤酒造 澤乃井)
address: Sawai, Ōme, Tokyo (a few steps from JR Sawai Station, on the Tama River)
w: Tokyo's oldest brewery, founded 1702 in the Okutama hills: free tours of kura buildings over 300 years old, then a tunnel to the riverside Sawanoi-en garden to taste ten sakes by the cup — plus a sake shop and tofu restaurants.

dish: Tamajiman sake and Tama no Megumi / Tokyo Blues craft beer, with pizza at Fussa no Birugoya
address: Fussa, Tokyo (near the Tama River, ~20 min walk from JR Haijima Station)
w: A sake brewery since 1863 (Tamajiman) that revived beer-making in 1998 after a 111-year pause — tour 19th-century kura and the Zougura museum, then drink Tama no Megumi or Tokyo Blues at the on-site Italian beer hall.

dish: Torisuki — chicken sukiyaki in a cast-iron nabe over a charcoal hibachi, the only dish on the menu
w: Founded in the last years of the 19th century and rebuilt after the 1923 earthquake in the two-storey timber house it still occupies: one dish only, chicken sukiyaki bubbling in a cast-iron pot over glowing charcoal.

dish: European-style beef curry on a fond-de-veau and demi-glace base simmered for days, with a fruity depth
n: Curry Bondy, Jimbōchō (欧風カレー ボンディ)
w: The Jimbōchō shop credited with creating 'European-style' curry — a roux built on veal stock and demi-glace simmered over days; up a flight above a bookshop, queues at lunch, and first winner of the Kanda Curry Grand Prix (2011).
